summary: extrahtml sdist fetches unpinned author-controlled dependency and mutable remote content at install time
details: The extrahtml 0.1.0 sdist ships no package code — top_level.txt is empty, SOURCES.txt lists only metadata plus setup.py, and src/ contains only egg-info. The only effect of installing it is setup.py's install-time behavior. setup.py calls subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', 'parseyaml>=1.2.0']) to fetch an unpinned, non-standard package named 'parseyaml' (not a recognized YAML library) outside normal dependency resolution, then imports it. It additionally retrieves https://raw.githubusercontent.com/optima1236/parsetxt/refs/heads/main/README.md over the mutable main branch with no hash or signature verification and passes the response bytes to parseyaml.safe_load. Both the parser code and the remote content are controlled by the same author and are unpinned, giving a remote code execution channel on every default pip install that builds the sdist (Linux glibc/musl x86_64 and aarch64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, Windows x86_64). The 'version check' framing is cover for the dropper: there is no shipped functionality that would justify an install-time network fetch and auxiliary-package install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
